name: Agno CodeMode toolkit (persistent IPython kernel)
pinned: agno 3.2.1 from PyPI with the [code] extra = agno-agi/agno tag v3.2.1 = 2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004 (clone at research/impls/agno-codemode/src; diff -r against the installed package differs only in three non-Python files). Runtime: ipykernel and jupyter_client from the extra, CPython 3.12.
engine: An ipykernel subprocess per session_id launched by jupyter_client with the host's own python and the host environment, talking ZeroMQ over localhost TCP. No sandbox: the module docstring says so.
how_run: CodeMode(tools=[lookup]) with lookup an async function; each execution awaits CodeMode.aexecute(RunContext(run_id, session_id), code), the model-facing method an Agent dispatches for the `execute` tool; ToolResult.content is what the model sees. AGNO_TELEMETRY=false before import. No LLM.

source_notes.finding: Injected tools become awaitable handles in the kernel namespace: a toolkit binds under its name minus '_tools', a plain callable under its own name. Binding is done by a bootstrap the host runs in the kernel; each kernel-side stub JSON-encodes its arguments and sends a comm message.

On demand: injected tools are removed from the model's tool schema and only their handle names go into the CodeMode instructions; the model calls help(handle) in the kernel to read signatures. That keeps schemas out of the prompt and scales past 100 tools (names only).

Kernel stub -> comm message on iopub -> the host's ToolBridge runs the tool's real FunctionCall (hooks, caching apply) under the cell's RunContext -> reply on the control channel (shell would deadlock while the cell runs). Async handles let asyncio.gather run calls concurrently (P9 229 ms). Tools that need confirmation or user input are refused inside the kernel.

None, by design and stated: 'CodeMode executes arbitrary Python and shell with the permissions of the process running the agent. It is not a sandbox'. Every call logs the same warning. Probes agree: network, /etc/hosts, PROBE_SECRET, file writes, `!` shell and os.system all work, also in the hardened config.
The model gets stdout, stderr, the last expression's repr (Out[n]) and any traceback, each capped at 65,536 chars with a visible omitted-chars marker.

Only a per-cell timeout, enforced by interrupting the kernel. If the interrupt does not land within interrupt_grace=1 s the call returns 'aborted' and the kernel keeps running; with on_busy_kernel='wait' (default) the next cell fails with KernelBusyError, with 'restart' the next cell restarts the kernel. No memory, CPU or tool-count limit.

One kernel per session_id, persistent across calls and runs in the same process (P8 persists); idle kernels evicted after idle_ttl=1800 s. With an fs=FileSystem, state is snapshotted as dill pickles and restored on resume, which the docstring notes is itself code execution.
The IPython traceback is returned as text with 'Cell In[1], line 2' and the message (P10). A dead kernel raises KernelDiedError out of execute instead of returning text.

Kernels run over TCP on 127.0.0.1 with random ports chosen by jupyter_client (stderr: 'Kernel is running over TCP without encryption'); messages are HMAC-signed with the connection key. CodeMode exposes no port or transport option, so this probe could not keep them inside its assigned 42000-42099 range. Telemetry to os-api.agno.com is on unless AGNO_TELEMETRY=false.

surprises: The time limit can be dodged: a cell that catches BaseException around its loop ignores the timeout's KeyboardInterrupt; execute returns '[cell aborted: the kernel did not respond to the interrupt in time and may still be running ...]' after 11.6 s while the kernel keeps one core at 100% (out/swallow_check.txt). With the default on_busy_kernel='wait' the next cell fails with KernelBusyError; with 'restart' the next cell kills it (out/swallow_check_hardened_restart.txt). Without a next cell it spins until idle eviction or process exit.

allow_shell=False reads like 'no shell' but only rejects cells that begin with %%bash and removes the bash cell magic; `!echo` (hardened-Pshell: SHELL-42), os.system and subprocess still run. The source comment is candid ('Footgun reducer, not a boundary', kernel.py:416-418); the parameter name and the instruction text are not.
env= cannot scrub the environment: it is merged over os.environ (kernel.py:391-392), so there is no option that hides host secrets from the kernel (hardened-P5: s3cr3t).

No memory limit: P7 reached 3.86 GB in 39 s before the kernel died from outside, and hardened P7 reached 3.97 GB in the 10 s before the timeout interrupted it. A death surfaces as an exception, not text for the model.
Kernels listen on random localhost TCP ports, unencrypted (HMAC-signed), outside any port range a host might assign.
